utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please be seated. May we please hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is case number IT-02-59-PT, the Prosecutor versus Darko Mrdja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Nicholas Koumjian, Sureta Chana, and Skye Winner for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Vojislav Dimitrijevic for the Defence of Mr. Mrdja. I don't know if this microphone is working properly, if somebody can fix it for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'll see that you get immediate assistance. Might I take the opportunity to ask the accused whether he understands the proceedings in a language he understands.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You may stay seated. I can see you have a lot of problems taking the microphone. So --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: At the same time, may I ask, do you have at this point in time any health problems or any complaint about the United Nations Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No complaints, Your Honour. Everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then let's follow the agenda of today. Pending motions, first of all. There was a motion filed by the Prosecution asking for the Judge's assistance for an identification parade. I took it from an answer in a separate motion that the Defence and the accused would be prepared to voluntarily participate in such a identification parade. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. But we make some remarks in order to clarify -- clarify the procedure of that line of procedure. Otherwise, we have no complaints, and the accused will participate in such line of procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the remaining question is really whether or not it's for the Pre-Trial Judge or the permanent Judges of the Chamber to respond to the request by the OTP. When you compare domestic laws, you will find the absence of rules on identification parades. In other countries you will -- for example, in the new Russian Code of Criminal Procedure you will find another solution just lining out, for example, that at least three if not five other persons of similar expression have to take part in such a line-up or identification parade that it has been video -- it has to be videoed and that the -- and this is the main purpose, that the Judges later mandated to hear the case, that they can follow these proceedings and that they can decide whether or not this was a real identification, was it a fair identification parade or not. But admittedly, I have never seen a rule saying that an identification parade would be such a coercive measure that a Judge -- a Judge's decision in advance would be necessary. So therefore, may I ask for the submission of the Prosecution why the Prosecution believes that it would be necessary to have the green light of the Pre-Trial Judge or the permanent Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, part of our concern was simply practical because we have to arrange with the Registry for the use of the facility and with the Detention Unit for the presence of the accused, and I think it would be extremely easier to do that with a court order than with a phone call from the Prosecutor saying we would like to do this. I really don't think the Detention Unit and Registry -- I'm sure their first response would be, "Do you have an order from the Judge?" So if it's not opposed, we would request it, and I would have some further remarks, requests to make of the Defence if they're willing, and that is that the accused have the appearance generally that the accused person did at the time, which was without facial hair. Just for the record, I would note that at the time of his arrest he did not have facial hair in his Initial Appearance but today has a significant amount of facial hair, and we think the probative value of the test of the identification parade would be enhanced and the value of that to the Judges. I'm not saying this can be compelled, but I'm requesting the cooperation of the Defence if the accused did not have facial hair when appearing in the line-up. But to directly answer your initial questions, because we're asking for the order in order to facilitate the cooperation of the Detention Unit and the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think based on this the Trial Chamber will leave it first for the Prosecution to do that what they feel appropriate in preparation, and I think we shouldn't interfere when there is no such special regulation providing for a judicial consent in advance. But maybe it's helpful for the Prosecution that as we did it in the past, I think we have to do everything what brings us closer to the truth, and of course in all legal systems such a line-up and identification parade is an appropriate way to come closer to the truth. And therefore, this attempt has the full support of this Trial Chamber, and I think we should only rule if any of the persons mentioned by you would not be prepared to cooperate. So therefore, we would leave it for the moment to the Prosecution to continue, and only if there are special obstacles, then it would be the time to rule on it. But for the moment I think we can't do more than that has been done already. As regards the question of the length or absence of hair, at that point or this point, I think this has to be discussed between the parties. In the moment I can't see any legal basis to compel Mr. Mrdja to do anything in this direction. But I had the impression that there is -- there could be a spirit of cooperation and this could be resolved in this way. I know it's not absolutely satisfactory for both parties, but in the absence of concrete rules and it has to be deplored that we don't have rules on these issues, in the moment I can see no legal basis for any such ruling. Any other comments on this issue? Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you, I'm sure, remember from the last Status Conference, I said that we want the clear procedure regarding this line-up procedure, prescribed procedure what the Prosecutor will do during that line-up procedure, and the Defence was provided with a draft of procedure and it is for me very strange that you have no copy of that piece of paper. We agreed with that -- with that kind of procedure, and the Prosecutor said that there will be six persons. And I will not describe any more procedure what was suggested by the Prosecutor. We had some comments on that but not substantial ones. So I will appreciate if the Prosecutor gets that paper about procedure of -- that line-up procedure to the Court as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We seem to be reading each other's minds, because about two minutes ago I asked Ms. Winner to have someone bring down a copy of that letter. So it's on its way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think I am in a totally different world. Now, normally the parties prefer not to have the Bench any kind of knowledge of what is happening amongst parties, but okay. But nevertheless, as I indicated beforehand, I can't see any legal basis for any kind of ruling and I have to invite the parties to come to an agreement on the procedure, and I would only feel honoured to rule as an arbiter in this case if there is no such an agreement. So please try to find out the appropriate solution, but I don't want to interfere now. If you need an arbiter, please contact me. Then the more honorary issues of such a Status Conference. I think there is no doubt that under Rule 66(A)(i) the disclosure was already completed before the last Status Conference to the satisfaction of the Defence. And then under Rule 66(A)(ii), the Defence was submitted with some material. Are there any problems emanating from Rule 66(A)(ii)? The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately we have the problems regarding Rule 66. Before the last Status Conference, the Prosecutor's Office just in that moment gets to us disclosure materials, but I didn't see it before and I must say that in supporting material with the indictment there is 17 statements of potential witnesses of the Prosecutor; among them 16 are with redacted names, surnames, and other data. Only one - and that one is judge of municipal court of Banja Luka, who is not witness who -- which appeared in supported material as a witness -- with his name, with full name. In this disclosure material we received statements from six witnesses with names and surnames, so the Prosecutor didn't comply with Rule 66, and I kindly ask the Court the set up a deadline for the Prosecutor to do so. We need names of witnesses, survivors and witnesses, with the victims and witnesses, because there are some survivors who are not witnesses in the Prosecutor case. We need to find -- at least to try to find those people. So I think that the Prosecutor didn't comply with Rule 66 at all. We -- I know that the Prosecutor last time said that there are circumstances which make to those witnesses and victims situation very dangerous if their names are on the record. I think that the Prosecutor -- the burden of proof is on the Prosecutor to give the evidence with which we shall see that such danger exists. We think that such danger doesn't exist under Rule 69. That Rule asks for exceptional circumstances, which doesn't exist in this matter. About Rule 68, I will talk after. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear observations by the Prosecution to this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution was going to submit a motion for protective measures for the witnesses. At this moment we've not done so because we still tried to discern which witnesses need not protection, but a lot of them asked for delayed disclosure, Your Honour, of their names. They have talked to our investigators and they have expressed concerns for their safety and their family's safety, and they do not wish their names to be disclosed at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: All right. This is my usual procedure, and we are looking forward to your motion, and only based on this and based on the reasons given there, no doubt we can decide on this. But to be quite clear beforehand, I take it that the line-up has to take place before the names are disclosed. And I have to tell the Defence at the same time that in some cases where the Chamber comes to the conclusion that a real danger for life or limb of a witness exists, that then the disclosure of the personal data of these persons should be disclosed only prior, of course in a time prior that you have time to do your work, prior to the hearing. We are in the unfortunate situation that -- I think it was already the second-last Status Conference there was a slight chance that there would be a time we know to hear this case. Unfortunately, it was not made possible. Later on it showed that it wouldn't have been possible to the -- for reasons of the health of one Judge. Then later on there was and to a certain extent there is still the idea to hear some smaller cases in a row; and therefore, it could be - but only it could be - that these cases could be heard somewhere later this year. But when I say "later this year," this means that the Defence can't expect that at the end of the day all the personal data of all the witnesses will be disclosed immediately. So we are looking forward for the motion by the Prosecution, and then witness by witness we will rule whether there are good reasons. But I would anticipate that one good reason is that these persons will participate in the line-up. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, in fact, Your Honour, one of the witnesses who will participate, I believe, would not object to his name being disclosed, and already his name has been disclosed. The other witnesses, they do ask that they not be visible to -- we do now have a letter. But the procedure we propose to the Defence is that the persons viewing the line-up not be visible to the accused. I know that particularly one of them has very deep concerns for his safety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be absolutely in line with international practice, that an accused can't see the persons. And I think this is already one good reason. But as you have heard, the Prosecution is aware that something has to be done, that they have to demonstrate whether or not we can apply Rule -- especially Rule 69 in this case, and we will rule on this as soon as possible and as soon as practicable. Any other comments to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: It's all right, Your Honour. We agree with that. Our main comment on line-up procedure was not in terms that accused can see witness, but we think that Defence counsel must be at the same side of the wall with the Prosecutor to see the witness. About explanation of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Step by step. Agreement with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sure about two of the three witnesses, and the last one I would just like to check with the witness, but I certainly understand counsel's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And this -- also, this would be in line with international practice. If not, exceptional circumstances prevail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: There are two groups, Your Honour, of witnesses. One is victims which survived that massacre; one group is witnesses who proceed to Travnik. Group of victims were publicly announced, names and surnames of those people in 1992 and in 1999. So we don't see any danger for those people to be announced which -- they missing only two persons, if I am correct. We agree with you that protective measures maybe are needed for some cases, but it is up to the Court, not to Prosecutor, to judge is the possibility to danger those victims or not. Now is March, the month of year, 2003. The first material was in June, year 2002. So I think that it is proper to set up the deadline for the Prosecutor's Office to disclose those materials, and if there is a motion for protective measures and if that motion is granted, it's all right with Defence that those witnesses will not be -- will not be disclosed to us. But not as a general rule, to have all witnesses without names and surnames. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Absolutely. We decide case by case. Would it be possible for the Prosecution to present the motion on this issue no later than the 17th of April? This is immediately before Easter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then Rule 68, any observations by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we requested a Rule 68 search of our computer database with certain criteria, and having checked this week apparently we were told we're at the -- still in a very long queue. We haven't gotten that back. I believe we have -- you know, as if any Rule 68 material becomes known to us, coming across or without the computer search, we will turn that over. But I can't off the top of my head think of any that has come across my -- that I've seen. And once we have -- if we do have a date from the Court, I know that then we could get some priority in that queue. But at the moment it's pending, it's in process, but the computer search has not been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We know these problems from nearly all cases, and you're absolutely right, priority will be given to those cases that are heard or even the cases close to the end of the hearing. And the criterion, the most important criterion, is no doubt when can this case be heard. As I don't want another time to give any estimate or to create any hopes on both sides, especially for Mr. Mrdja, who has a right to have -- and to be heard as promptly as possible. But for the calculation within the framework of the bureau, what has priority, which cases can be heard in the near future, I would ask once again the Prosecution. What is, from your point of view, as it stands now, the estimated length of the Prosecution case? Once we heard you would call 15 to 17 witnesses, some 92 bis statements, and the Prosecution's case would be about four to six weeks. Is it still correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think that was a very conservative estimate. I think it will be that or shorter. I think realistically we could put it on within four weeks, our case. We have -- this is a slightly different subject, but we have asked the Defence to consider an agreed facts regarding the prerequisites under Articles 3 and 5, that there was an armed conflict and widespread and systematic attack. If we do get that, those agreed facts, then even the number of 92 bis statements will become minimal, and we will just proceed to evidence regarding what happened on the 21st of August. If we do not get that, it will only mean that we'll present a lot of evidence by way of 92 bis. We do not anticipate calling live witnesses to establish those facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This brings me already to the next point in line. And I recall that at the last Status Conference the Defence told us that you would need about another 45 days before negotiations on agreed facts could be started with the Prosecution. May I ask what is the development? Is it the Defence case that this chapeau element of crime be contested, or is it possible to come to agreed facts at least as regards the question of armed conflict coming to the other elements later?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, I want to apologise. And maybe on the end, if you allow, to discuss -- to maybe get back on previous point on 66(B). Maybe I forgot. If you allow me. But regarding this particular question, I can say that yesterday we received a paper from -- a document from the Prosecutor's Office, and their proposal what facts can be agreed. I didn't have an opportunity to discuss that issue with my client, but I am pretty much sure that some kind of agreement will be reached at this point. If you can allow me to discuss about 68. I didn't have an opportunity to talk about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'll come to this -- to this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But in fact, the core problem is would the Defence, of course with the -- the consent of Mr. Mrdja in person, would you accept following the long line of decisions handed down by this Tribunal, would you accept that at that period of time there was an armed conflict and there was a widespread and systematic attack?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said to you a few minutes Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 52 to 56. before, I received that letter from the Prosecutor yesterday, and I had no opportunity to discuss that issue with my client. As a matter of fact, we tried to discuss that with the Prosecutor's Office in my visit in December, but I didn't find anybody -- or Mr. Koumjian, I didn't find at the office at that time. And we are eager to cooperate with the Prosecutor on that issue, and I'm sure that we shall reach agreement on those facts but, please, I cannot today make any statements about those facts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask the parties to notify the Trial Chamber no later, once again, than the 17th of April whether or not it was possible for you to come to agreed facts, especially related to the question of an armed conflict and the question of a widespread and systematic attack. This would facilitate our work and it might open - I don't want to propose anything - but it might open a time window for this case. You wanted to raise another issue related to 66 -- 66(B). Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Thank you, Your Honour. We didn't receive any item which will be as evidence or, if any, from the Prosecutor through paragraph -- Rule 66(B). We are interested, especially in photographs, which maybe the Prosecutor possess and other -- other items if they have it. But we didn't receive anything. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That's a reasonable request, and I'll try to review the -- all the evidence that we've planned to present. And any photographs that we have of the site will be handed over to Mr. Dimitrijevic. We have photographs taken years after the event. But as Your Honour is aware, from seeing some of them in the Stakic case, we do have photographs of the site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You can accept this, that it -- I think it will be done in due time. So this shouldn't be a problem at all. As regards the question of the trial date, I mentioned already the problems we are facing in the moment. And it really depends on the question whether it can be done in a very short period of time. "Very short" here in this Tribunal would mean four weeks for the Prosecution, and I don't know what would be the time the Defence would need. But then taking into account that also a judgment has to be written, Ad Litem Judges have to be assigned to the case, the overall -- the shortest possibility would be about three months. But prerequisite would be as soon as possible - really as soon as possible - we get the information from the parties that they are proceeding -- prepared to proceed in this way and maybe even come to other agreed facts going beyond the question of widespread and systematic attack and beyond the question of an armed conflict. Maybe in this case really the evidence provided by the Prosecution might convince the Defence that a certain approach is more appropriate than the other, to put it very carefully. We have to come to the question of counsel. And there was a request during the last Status Conference on the appointment of co-counsel. As to the fact that we have to come back to some exchange of letters between the Registry and counsel, I think it would be appropriate to discuss this issue in private session. Do the parties agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then let's please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It may be surprising but -- to raise this issue right now, but it was part of your request during the last Status Conference that you raised a question of a co-counsel in your case. Did you come closer to a maybe solution or suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, from time being I think that in this phase of pre-trial procedure Mr. Mrdja don't need co-counsel. If co-counsel will be needed a few months or two before the trial, so in that stage we shall ask the Registry to appoint co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clear and fair answer. Any other issues? We learned the pre-trial brief could be handed down as soon as possible in case parties come to agreed facts. Any other issues to be raised from the side of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the side of the Defence or the accused in person?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence filed the motion for provisional release of Mr. Mrdja. I don't know if you received that. And we want to know what is scheduled about discussing and making decisions in that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before I give the floor to the Prosecution, you mentioned guarantees given by Bosnia-Herzegovina, in this case the entity of Republika Srpska. They arrived a long, long time ago, and we were surprised to receive the guarantees first and then only a long time later your request. You gave reasons why you didn't file a motion on provisional release. I haven't discussed this issue yet with my colleagues. We'll do as soon as possible. And I can tell you already that if there are not urgent reasons demonstrated by the Defence, this would not be a case where a hearing on this motion should be necessary, because we have all the facts before us and not much can be added. We have the guarantees. The question may be whether they have to be updated or renewed because they are already -- they stem from a period sometime ago. This would be a separate matter, but this could be resolved without any hearing. But may I ask the Prosecution, has the Prosecution already a clear view on the response to this motion? Because you know that my policy is to avoid unnecessary filings. And if you could comment on this issue already today, this would be of great assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The position of the Prosecution is that we will be opposing this motion for provisional release and we'll be filing our response before the due date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you share the view that no oral hearing will be necessary?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We are of the view that no oral should be necessary in this, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I then take the opportunity at the same time, if the Defence agrees, to ask Mr. Mrdja in person whether or not he wants to add some personal remarks to the question of provisional release, because I believe it's the right whenever an accused wants to address on this issue of deprivation or liberty the Chamber in person. Mr. Mrdja, do you want to make any additional statements? You may stay seated. It's too problematic for you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we need new microphones here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing. Your Honour, I have nothing to add. I just have one problem, and that is that my child is very sick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is reflected in the motion filed by the Defence and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that everything has been filed, but my attorney will contact you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any other issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then I have to thank you. And I'm looking forward to all the motions. We learnt that they would arrive in the near future. And this concludes today's Status Conference in this case.
